f1.quote: The modulation period (individual layer thickness, λ) was varied among 8, 16, 32, and 80 nm by RF magnetron sputtering to create multilayers dominated respectively by coherent heterointerfaces (M8), semicoherent heterointerfaces (M16), or grain boundaries (M32 and M80), followed by nanoindentation c

f2.quote: Room-temperature nanoindentation used a 5 mN maximum load, loading rates of 1, 0.1, and 0.01 mN/s

f3.quote: a 100 s hold, and 20 s unloading; indentation depths were maintained at approximately 1/10–1/7 of the coating thickness

f4.quote: Deposition used a base pressure of about 5 × 10^-4 Pa, Ar flow of 100 sccm, working pressure of 0.3 Pa, 150 W on the HEA target, alternating 0/30 W on the Al target, and a 1 h deposition.

f8.quote: a transition from dislocation-mediated creep to atomic-diffusion- or interface-slip-mediated creep

f9.quote: Relative to multilayers dominated by coherent interfaces or grain boundaries, the λ = 16 nm semicoherent multilayer exhibits the greatest room-temperature creep resistance

f10.quote: the λ = 16 nm semicoherent multilayer exhibits the greatest room-temperature creep resistance and a transition from dislocation-mediated creep to atomic-diffusion- or interface-slip-mediated creep

f11.quote: M8 (λ = 8 nm, coherent interfaces) and M32/M80 (λ = 32/80 nm, grain-boundary-dominated interfaces), which show predominantly dislocation-mediated creep
